ownership: The partial sort path borrows the rational manager, copies coefficient numerals into typed owned buffer slots, sorts scalar IDs, then swaps each raw numeral with its source-indexed slot. A whole-slice raw swap transfers numeral ownership between the equation slice and buffer without cloning.

The concrete equation allocates its owner header first, copies coefficients into indexed reusable slots, transfers them into its vectors with sort_core, then owns its constant, integer coefficients and rational justifications. del_eq releases those in that order, leaving caller inputs and reusable buffers separately owned.

The pre-elimination setup borrows its rational manager, publishes variable metadata before the matching integer buffer slot, reserves that ID in a concrete solved-index-priority heap, publishes a justification buffer slot before incrementing its ID, owns equation pointers in source list order, and closes its heap, rational and integer member buffers in reverse declaration order.

Solved-equation promotion transfers one equation pointer from the todo list to the solution list. apply_solution swaps integer and rational row storage through reusable owned numeral buffers; the old target row remains in its buffer until the next reset or solver destruction. The coefficient borrowed from that old row remains alive across the rational merge.

Non-unit decomposition borrows the selected positive magnitude, publishes a new parameter and buffer slot, compacts the todo equation's remainder numerals in place, copies auxiliary coefficients from the owned decomposition buffer into a solution equation, then substitutes that solution into prior occurrences. The decomposition buffer releases its copied numerals after the solution has independent ownership.
deviations: Source normalize_eq checks divisibility of the constant but divides only variable coefficients and justification coefficients by their gcd. The Go path retains that exact result. After source normalize_eq destroys an empty zero equality, assert_eq still calls add_occs on its null slot; Go skips that invalid dereference.

Unit and non-unit elimination, internal solve, normalize query and public solver methods now have concrete Go paths. Source svector::erase(value) ignores an absent occurrence, which happens for a decomposition parameter in the compacted original equation; Go matches this no-op. Explanation IDs are returned as a copy of the source const vector, and io.Writer reports host write errors. Whole-source error/debug/driver audit remains open.

ownership: The mutable interval and node bounds own their fast-float endpoints; constant interval views borrow current node bounds. The context owns its root, parameter numerals and copied polynomial coefficients, and borrows the numeric manager and resource limit.

Fast inequalities own copied scoped fast-float values through their context. Clauses borrow atom pointers, count source-style references and register each watched variable once; context close retires the owning values after nodes. Learned-clause deletion and justification lifetime remain open.

Root close precedes source-order unit then problem-clause then lemma reference release; shared inequality values close at their last reference, and remaining unreferenced context-owned values close before context numerals. Idempotent release progress preserves cleanup retries.
deviations: The config_mpff tactic variable registration now grows source-order type/watch slots and the Go root bound arrays before initialization. The config_mpff root unit/definition/queue initialization and shared clause teardown are concrete. Selected bound justification tags are ported; node search/splitting, complete explanation ownership and the full solver lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff six named parameter updates now retain source order, defaults, partial numeric mutation and a closable refused owner. The Go context allocates its root before this pass; complete constructor allocation order, node search/splitting and full solver lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff context now displays definitions, units and clauses through the source MPFF to_rational_string spelling, which delegates to the ordinary String formatter. Borrowed variable display and shell forwarding are concrete; search remains open.

The config_mpff context now records child creation order, displays consistent leaves with inherited bounds and exact MPFF numeral text, and omits conflicting leaves. Search, splitting and statistics remain open.

The config_mpff round-robin variable selector and midpoint splitter now use concrete FastFloat arithmetic. Integer-bound normalization, directed unbounded splits and adjacent-value refusal preserve source order; the enclosing search queue, depth/node budgets and full tactic lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff search loop now initializes the root, selects leaves breadth-first, replays child decisions, resumes canceled propagation, enforces depth/node limits and owns split children through cleanup. Fast and arbitrary-float checkpoints read their numeric Runtime when no shared process is bound, and read ProcessAccounting when it is bound; the pointer-free hardware context needs an explicit process binding. Standalone runtimes cannot include allocations from unrelated owners, and the complete tactic result/simplify lifecycle remains open.

remaining TRACE_CODE/TRACE/STRACE/CTRACE call-site emission

ownership: TraceTags owns a native Go map of C-string tag values; Finalize drops that table but preserves enable-all. The gparams, shell -tr option and public API tag controls share the process singleton; the full shell driver and API logging/memory initialization remain open. An injected trace writer is borrowed; the _TRACE process owner opens .z3-trace when the package loads, while an explicitly constructed unbound owner opens it on first emission.
deviations: Retained trace controls use native map tag state with C-string keys, lazy table initialization and source finalize/all-flag order. The g3trace build gate erases emission in ordinary builds; all four gparams.cpp TRACE sites are wired. No retained source caller invokes open_trace or close_trace. Cooperation checkpoint TRACE and CTRACE plus integer divides STRACE and TRACE and integer negation, add/sub/mul and division-wrapper and rational add/sub/mul, mixed and division STRACE plus MPF sqrt-helper and MPFF lt, add/sub, mul, div, floor/ceil and power STRACE plus set_core, add_sub, mul, div, power and to_mpq TRACE are wired; MPBQ rational-lower select_small and debug-only add/sub TRACE plus MPQ parser set TRACE are wired; other optional TRACE/STRACE/CTRACE call sites remain open.

MPN div_n TRACE emits every source-defined insertion through the opening numerator bracket. The next C++ display_raw read requests limb m+n from a logical m+n buffer and is undefined; Go returns arena.ErrBounds at that boundary, suppressing later borrow/newline/footer output. This is the complete defined behavior of this reached call site, not a port of the invalid read.
